items.name: Buff-banded rail
items.text: A striped, chicken-sized bird that dashes across the boardwalk. Hard to miss, and bold around people. Please don't feed it.

items.name: Emerald dove
items.text: Glossy green wings and a soft call. Usually heard rustling through leaf litter on the forest floor before it is seen.

items.name: Silvereye
items.text: Tiny olive-green birds with a white eye-ring, darting about the canopy in busy flocks.

items.name: Pied imperial-pigeon
items.text: Large white pigeons that arrive in the summer months. Their soft calls fill the canopy during the forest fruiting season.

items.name: Osprey
items.text: A fish-eating raptor that soars over the reef flat and plunges feet-first for fish.

items.name: White-bellied sea-eagle
items.text: A huge white and grey eagle with broad, upswept wings. Watch for it soaring above the beach walk.

items.name: Oystercatchers
items.text: Black or black-and-white shorebirds with long red bills, probing the sand along the shoreline.

items.name: Egrets & reef herons
items.text: Tall white herons that stalk the shallows. Look for them from the jetty and along the tide line.

items.name: Terns
items.text: Slender seabirds that hover and dive for small fish. More than 35 seabird species are recorded around the island.

items.name: Green turtle
items.text: Drawn to Green Island's undulating seagrass beds. Watch the surface from the jetty for a head popping up to breathe.

items.name: Stingrays
items.text: Scan the sandy bottom below the jetty. Stingrays send up a cloud of sand as they dart away.

items.name: Pelagic fish
items.text: Large fish live under the jetty, gliding in and out of its shadows.

items.name: Reef fish
items.text: Colourful reef fish crowd the coral bommies visible from the jetty and on a snorkel.

items.name: Hard & soft corals
items.text: More than 190 kinds of hard coral and over 100 soft corals, grading from shallow to deep water. Never stand on coral; use rest stations.

items.name: Seagrass meadows
items.text: Shallow meadows that shelter juvenile fish and feed turtles and dugongs.

items.name: Dugong
items.text: A shy marine mammal that grazes on seagrass. A rare and lucky sighting.

items.name: Sea cucumber (bêche-de-mer)
items.text: Harvested and smoked on the island from 1857. Today it is protected, like everything in this no-take zone.

items.name: Vine-thicket rainforest
items.text: Dense, shady rainforest growing in sand in the island's centre. Green Island is the only one of about 300 reef cays with rainforest.

items.name: Coastal she-oak (casuarina)
items.text: Wispy, needle-like foliage that frames the day-use area. Tolerates sand, salt and wind, sheltering the rainforest.

items.name: Beach almond
items.text: Broad leaves that turn red before they fall. One of the salt-tolerant plants that shield the island interior.

items.name: Coconut palm
items.text: The swaying palms of the day-use area. Coconuts were planted here in 1889.

items.name: Pandanus
items.text: Screw pines with stilt roots and spiral leaves, typical of reef-island shores.

items.name: Saltwater crocodile
items.text: See them up close at Marineland Melanesia, which began as a crocodile farm in 1964.
